rationale: This change modifies only contracts/security-audit/package-lock.json, moving transitive development dependency fast-uri from 3.1.8 to 3.1.9. The lockfile is tooling, not declared contract content. metadata.contract, metadata.schema_version and compatibility_policy are reused unchanged; no event, schema, policy, registry or fixture is redefined. This assessment was authored for original replacement candidate 7dc8aed1bfda8324fbf8d691fe3e4340ad3ff1ca. The owner has since merged the dependency via #888; the rebased integration changes only these OpenSpec records and is not retroactive assessment or authority for that implementation.
trust_boundary: No trust boundary moves. fast-uri stays dev: true and is loaded only when the contract tests compile the generated schema with AJV; nothing crosses a process, network or tenancy boundary at runtime, and no shipped artifact changes. The governance boundary is unchanged: the lockfile was already the one path contract.toolchainExemptions exempts from the frozen-contract prefix rule.
transformation_ownership: No transformation is added, removed or relocated. The canonical contract source keeps sole ownership of event identity and shape, the contract generator keeps sole ownership of the generated artifacts, and check-contract-immutability.mjs keeps sole ownership of proving that every path contract-provenance.json declares is unchanged.

alternatives.rejection_reason: Extending security-audit@2.1.0 would claim a contract change in order to remediate a dev dependency advisory. The advisory is in the test toolchain, and no contract input or output changes, so no compatibility classification applies.
A new contract would redefine scope to move a transitive development dependency; the requested update introduces no contract semantics.

author.name: Codex, under direct instruction from Fernando Homem da Costa
